values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations or fee. Monongahela rules: no more than 14 cumulative days at one site within a 28-day period, then move more than 5 road miles or wait 21 days; vehicles must stay on or adjacent to roads open to public travel. Camping is prohibited within 300 ft (slope distance) of the Lake Buffalo shore except at Forest Service developed campsites.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/alerts/general-use-restrictions (Forest Order: 'Camping outside developed campgrounds at any one campsite in excess of fourteen (14) cumulative days within a 28-day period, then relocating the camp within five (5) road miles of the site just occupied without a waiting period of three weeks (21 days)') + Monongahela NF release reprinted by Parsons Advocate 2023-04-24 (https://parsonsadvocate.com/news/pa-top-stories/headlines/monongahela-national-forest-issues-reminder-about-camping-and-food-storage-regulations/: dispersed camping 'is free of charge anywhere in the national forest outside of a designated campground'; 'All vehicles must remain on or adjacent to roadways that are open to public travel') + same order item 19: 'Camping within 300 feet (slope distance)of the shores of Lake Buffalo, Spruce Knob Lake, Summit Lake, and Lake Sherwood, excluding Forest Service Developed campsites', read 2026-10-22

summary: The Forest Service's Lake Buffalo page (updated 2026-03-23) describes a 22-acre trout lake with parking, picnic area and boat ramp, 'Open, except when roads closed by snow', toilets closed in winter, no potable water, and says only that 'there are dispersed campsites in the area'. Booking set from the forest's dispersed-camping rules: first-come, no reservations, 14 days in 28, plus the order banning camping within 300 ft of the Lake Buffalo shore (overrides the inherited recreation.gov row). Fees ($0, AWH/manual), hookups and season (from AWH's note) left. Note unchanged.
flags: Missing website: the Forest Service page https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/lake-buffalo (Greenbrier Ranger District). Missing phone: Greenbrier Ranger District, Bartow office, (304) 456-3335 (2023 Forest release).

Name/character: no Forest Service page designates a 'Lake Buffalo Recreation Area' camping area; the FS page names the day-use site 'Lake Buffalo' and says only 'For those looking for an extended stay there are dispersed campsites in the area', and the forest's list of developed-dispersed camping areas (Greenbrier RD: Little River FR 17, Mower Tract FR 227/235, Stonecoal FR 209, West Fork FR 44) does not include it.

Legality near the lake: Forest Order item 19 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/alerts/general-use-restrictions) prohibits 'Camping within 300 feet (slope distance)of the shores of Lake Buffalo ... excluding Forest Service Developed campsites'. Consistent with AWH's 'Campsites do not appear to be lakefront'; any lakeside spot would be unlawful.

Season: AWH's note says 'open from March to November'; the FS page says the site is 'Open, except when roads closed by snow. End toilet and trash service on 12/1', and the 2026 opening list gives 'Lake Buffalo— 4/15'. Neither speaks for the dispersed sites; season (year_round false, derived from the note) and the AWH text left as they are.

Road, for information: Forest Service road layer (queried 2026-10-22): the pin sits on NFSR 54 'BUFFALO FORK' / 54A, maintenance level '3 - SUITABLE FOR PASSENGER CARS', gravel. FS directions: 'take Forest Rd. for 2.5 miles and the parking area will be on your right'. No agency vehicle-length, high-clearance or 4WD statement.
